engagement_title: Kilnmore range relaunch: bring two mornings of bench captures to one house look, recover the inked mark as real artwork, rebuild the printer's line sheet into a live merge, and hand the storefront and the wholesale room one editable set
vertical: E-commerce, Retail and Product: a small matte glaze ceramics label selling direct through its own online storefront and to independent home goods stockists (Portland, Maine)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'Graphic designer, advertising creatives' open call from a direct to consumer homeware brand wanting 'high-performing static ad creatives, promotional graphics, and multiple creative variations for testing across our paid social campaigns', working 'from existing brand guidelines', with 'clean, modern, conversion-focused visuals'. Co-anchors: the Freelancer.com brief from a small shop wanting a product photographer for ten to fifteen catalogue shots and a logo, honestly re-cast here as the post production half a product photographer actually does at the desk, since the connector cannot operate a camera and cannot draw a mark from scratch, so the client sends its own raw captures and a photographed hand inked mark; the Freelancer.com brief from a vendor with 'product descriptions and a clean image set already prepared' needing the specification bearing catalogue material a retail intake team approves, repositioned to record per page because a multi product grid catalogue is not producible on this surface; and the Freelancer.com 'Modern Store Graphics Package' brief for an online shop refreshing its storefront with a hero banner sized for desktop and for mobile, product detail assets plus iconography, and section graphics, art directed as 'clean lines, bold but balanced color, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy', with layered source files requested alongside the exports. Laundered to the fictional Kilnmore; no real company, person, marketplace, platform or trademark appears.
client_one_liner: Fourteen frames shot across two very different mornings, a mark that exists only as a photograph of brushed ink, a line sheet the printer built and we cannot open, and a whole relaunch that has to look like one line.
client_brief:
Kilnmore, range relaunch.

We make matte glaze ceramics in a small studio and we sell two ways: direct through our own online storefront, and wholesale to independent home goods shops. We are relaunching the range and we would rather one person carried the whole thing than have the pieces come back from four people looking like four brands.

The photography is ours. We shot the range on the bench by the studio window over two mornings and it is honest but it is not consistent. We need the pieces to look like one line, and we need the glazes to still be the glazes: the oatmeal has to stay oatmeal, the ash has to stay ash, the cobalt slip has to stay cobalt. That is what people are buying and it is what gets returned when it is wrong.

Our mark is a brush drawing. It was inked on a tile years ago and all we have is a photograph of it. We need it back as artwork we can actually use at any size, on a label, on a banner, on the front of a line sheet.

Then the pieces. Product page tiles for each piece: the hero, the detail, and one that carries the specifications. A set for the paid campaigns at the three shapes we run, and each one has to make a different argument for a different piece rather than being the same picture cropped three ways. Storefront graphics: the wide banner and the tall one, section graphics and small icons that tie the pages together. A wholesale deck for the buyer meetings with the line sheet prices in it. A one page look at the range, and a short page showing the mark and the type so the next person does not guess.

And the line sheets themselves. The printer produced those last season off our own data, one piece per page. We have their file and nothing else. Keep it looking exactly as it does and put this season's range, dimensions and prices through it.

A mug is thirty four dollars, a dinner set is one hundred and eighty, wholesale is about half. Calm, full frame, plenty of space, nothing fussy. Send it back as one file we can edit, and tell us if anything in our data looks wrong before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Mugs 34 dollars, bowls 42 dollars, a serving platter 96 dollars, a four piece dinner set 180 dollars; wholesale at roughly half of retail with a six piece opening minimum. Two audiences: direct buyers aged 28 to 50 who own two or three considered kitchen objects and are choosing between this and a comparable studio line, and independent home goods stockists whose buyers judge a range on whether the line sheet is legible and complete enough to order from. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is calm and full frame: one piece given room, a house neutral that does not move between tiles, dimensions and prices set plainly in the run of the sheet, and space used as the argument. Push it toward impulse marketplace grammar, a tiled grid of nine pieces, price flashes, a countdown strip, three exclamation colours, and a thirty four dollar mug reads as an eight dollar mug and a wholesale buyer closes the sheet, which is the exact commercial failure the client is describing when they say calm and nothing fussy. Push it the other way into gallery austerity with the pieces small and the type tiny and a buyer cannot read the dimensions they need to order from. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,600 dollars fixed, or 45 to 75 dollars an hour across 35 to 55 hours.

brand_identity.sector: A small matte glaze ceramics studio selling direct through its own online storefront and wholesale to independent home goods stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2015, Portland, Maine, a two partner studio working at one bench by the window.
brand_identity.about: Kilnmore makes matte glaze ceramics for everyday use: mugs, bowls, a serving platter, dinner sets. We sell direct through our own storefront and wholesale to independent home goods shops with a six piece opening minimum. The pieces are quiet and full framed, and the glaze is the point. Oatmeal, ash, cobalt slip and bare clay are what a buyer chooses and what a stockist orders against, so they have to stay true wherever they appear.
brand_identity.audience: Direct buyers aged 28 to 50 who own two or three considered kitchen objects and are choosing between us and a comparable studio line, and independent home goods stockists whose buyers judge a range on whether the line sheet is legible and complete enough to order from.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mugs 34 dollars, bowls 42 dollars, serving platter 96 dollars, four piece dinner set 180 dollars. Wholesale at roughly half of retail. Considered studio ceramics, not impulse marketplace and not gallery austerity.
brand_identity.typography: One warm, legible system: a quiet humanist serif for the mark, headings and range names, paired with a clean sans for the specification tables and dimensions so a stockist reads them without effort. Warmth without decoration, nothing script, nothing ornamented.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and warm, the studio talking about its own work. Example line the brand would write: Thrown and glazed in small batches, made to be used every day. No sale language, no urgency, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark is a brush drawing inked years ago onto an unglazed clay tile, and the only version that exists is a photograph of that tile on the bench. There is no working file. The mark has to be recovered from the photograph as artwork the studio can use at any size before the relaunch can carry it. The written guideline survives, plus a phone snap of the shop counter kept as a warmth reference.
brand_identity.values: Honest materials shown plainly, and one line that reads as one line across every piece and every page.

assets_supplied.name: range_captures/ (14 frames, 4200 x 2800)
assets_supplied.kind: The studio's own captures of thirteen pieces on the workbench by the window, shot across two mornings on the same linen backdrop.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Two mornings on the same bench with the same cloth. Honest, but not consistent.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One morning was flat overcast and the other was direct sun, so the glazes read at two different temperatures and the sun morning's glaze breaks are fully clipped, which means an attempt to recover them reports success while nothing in the picture moves. Separately, the oatmeal and ash pieces sit at almost the same value as the linen behind them, so an isolation of those pieces reports success and quietly bites the rim, and the pieces with closed handles keep the linen trapped inside the handle void.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_mark_tile.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the studio's hand inked mark, brushed years ago onto an unglazed clay tile that now sits on the bench.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'The mark as it was originally inked on a tile. It is the only version that exists.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The brushed ink and the unglazed clay it sits on are close in value, so a selection that names the tile returns the tile rather than the ink and every downstream step then works on a rectangle. The ligature in the mark encloses a counter that a one call knockout fills with captured clay while reporting complete success.

assets_supplied.name: linesheet_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of last season's wholesale line sheet, US Letter portrait, one piece per page, fonts embedded, produced from the studio's own data through a full print engine. Carries a piece photograph, a name and description block, a nine row specification table, a care and firing note and both prices.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'What the printer sent us last season. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was put together. Keep it exactly as it is.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The specification table came out of the studio's system as one continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per parameter frames to map and everything has to be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. The readout of that story silently omits the run holding the care and firing note while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator still reports valid, and the fields past the omission never become placeholders at all.

assets_supplied.name: range_data.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export of the season's range, one row per piece, with columns for piece code, name, description, nine specification parameters, care and firing note, retail price, wholesale price and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Our range data. The dimensions and the care note are what a stockist orders against, so they are held to as written.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Fifteen rows for thirteen live pieces: two discontinued glazes the system still emits, flagged only by a retired column the client never mentions. Two pieces have their dimensions entered in centimetres while the rest are in inches, with no unit marker anywhere in the row, and the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires.

assets_supplied.name: brand_notes.txt plus counter_2024.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A page of the studio's existing written guideline, plus a phone snap of the shop counter kept as a warmth reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Clean lines, balanced colour, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy. And a picture of our counter, because that warmth is the thing we keep losing when someone else designs for us.'

acceptance_bar: All thirteen pieces read as one line shot on one morning, judged with the range laid out together rather than one piece at a time.
The four glazes stay distinguishable from each other and none has been pushed toward a colour the glaze is not. Oatmeal stays oatmeal, ash stays ash, cobalt slip stays cobalt.
Every product page tile shows the whole piece at a consistent scale across the range. A tile that shows part of a piece is a rejected tile even if it is a good picture.
Cutouts are cut on the piece's own edge, with nothing bitten out of a rim and no backdrop left trapped inside a handle.
The mark comes back as artwork that scales, sits clean and transparent on any ground, and keeps its enclosed counter open at the sizes we use it.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

Line sheets: exactly one page per live piece, every field the 2025 sheet carried present on every page, every value bound verbatim from our export, and the photograph on each page the piece named on that page.

Nothing in our export may be shortened, reworded, converted or abbreviated to make it fit or to make it consistent. Anything that looks wrong to you, raise it in writing rather than fixing it quietly.
The press file renders at real print resolution at US Letter trim, and there is one sheet file per piece named to the piece code, containing the piece its name claims.
The paid set makes three different arguments for three different pieces. The same picture at three shapes is a rejected set.

The wholesale deck, the paid set, the storefront banners, the spec tile, the range one pager and the mark and type page come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own fixed size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text, the line sheet price table is a real table and the mark and icons are real artwork we can change, not pictures of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, anything in our export you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the sheet could not carry.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The line sheets are one piece per page against a layout the client has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The banners, deck, paid set and pages need several fixed canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring, and they must be authored as fixed canvases rather than as one adaptive layout. The product tiles are photography and come out of the imaging surface as real files.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the fourteen captures, the inked mark photograph, the 2025 line sheet PDF and the range export, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline. Thirty artefacts later the mapping between URL, piece code and role has to still be trustworthy, and fourteen frames do not correspond one to one with thirteen pieces.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by piece and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen captures and the mark photograph and triage: which morning, which glaze, how level, how much the piece separates from the linen behind it, whether closed handles enclose a void, and whether the piece in each frame is the piece its data row claims.
trajectory.judgement: The client describes an inconsistency problem. The agent also has to read which pieces sit at the same value as their background before deciding how anything is derived from those frames, and to read the export against the pictures rather than assuming a fifteen row export describes thirteen pieces.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering morning, glaze, level, separation, enclosed voids and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes every crop decision rather than following one.

trajectory.action: Fix one house neutral from the better morning and correct each capture toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame and what refused to move.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across fourteen frames rather than fourteen locally pleasing pictures. The sun morning needs a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral, and where its glaze breaks are fully clipped a recovery attempt returns success with nothing changed, which is information about what the frame can still carry rather than a reason to push harder.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log and a note of what did not respond.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to keep the four glazes apart: hold oatmeal out of yellow, keep ash from collapsing into the linen, keep cobalt slip saturated without going purple, keep bare clay warm.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one, since the glaze is what is being bought and what gets returned. Prompt wording is the whole gate, and a material selection on a pale matte piece against a pale linen can leak into the linen, which has to be read as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Glaze protected masters with the masked parameters recorded per piece.

trajectory.action: Derive the product page hero and detail crops for every piece, reading the detection confidence and the tradeoffs each crop returns rather than trusting success, then lay the heroes out together as the range page they are for.
trajectory.judgement: Consistent piece scale across thirteen tiles is a set level decision that cannot be made one tile at a time, and a subject aware crop is a guess with a confidence attached that lives in the response rather than in the picture.
trajectory.produces: Hero and detail crops per piece, laid out as the range, with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.action: Isolate the range onto the chosen tile ground, routing per piece, then look at every cutout on that ground at real tile size.
trajectory.judgement: A one call knockout is right for a dark cobalt piece standing clear of the linen and is a different proposition on a pale matte piece against pale linen, and the route is a per piece decision made by looking at the piece rather than a setting applied to the range.
trajectory.produces: Thirteen isolations on the tile ground with the route recorded per piece.

trajectory.action: Recover the inked mark: a selection naming the ink's own visual properties rather than the tile it sits on, invert, crop to the mask's own bounds, trace to SVG, inject a viewBox, strip the opaque full canvas path, and produce the transparent raster variant alongside it.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle. The trace ships with no viewBox and an opaque background rectangle and neither is announced, and the enclosed counter in the ligature is the part a knockout would fill while reporting success.
trajectory.produces: The mark as scalable transparent vector artwork plus a transparent raster variant.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the range export against the photography and the written guideline, normalise it into a merge shaped file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the sheet masters and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data preparation work: retired rows the system still emits, an image column that does not satisfy the contract, and two rows whose dimensions are in different units from the rest with nothing in the row to say so. The acceptance bar forbids quietly converting them, so the agent decides what is its call and what is the client's, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 line sheet to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the studio's own system happened to produce rather than by the plan. Two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, and deciding which holds the piece photograph is a judgement made against the printed reference rather than against a name in the response.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every specification field, the care note, both prices and the photograph, ordering any rows that share a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, computing offsets from a source of truth chosen deliberately rather than from whichever readout was handed over, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the sheet fields and the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before any page exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per piece photographs bound, render the press file and 300 ppi proofs at trim, produce per piece sheets named to the piece code, and read every rendered page against its export row at true trim.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to a press file forfeits the per record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming thirteen sheets by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a stockist discovers while ordering.
trajectory.produces: The press sheet file, 300 ppi proofs, per piece identity verified sheets, and a page by page reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one table or interior context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the range.
trajectory.judgement: A thumbnail is not a photograph. The frame has to be judged where it will live, at full resolution and adjacent to the graded range, against a house neutral that was fixed days earlier and a set of glazes that must not be argued with by whatever crockery the frame contains.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to carry the warmth the client says it keeps losing while staying legible in a nine row specification table. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML holding the wholesale deck roots with the line sheet price table as a real table, the three paid canvases each making its own argument for its own piece, the wide and tall storefront banner canvases as fixed sizes, the specification tile, the range one pager and the mark and type page carrying the recovered mark and the icon set as inline vector. Each root declares its own canvas size, every photograph is base64 inlined, family and weight are declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and every other canvas through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition resolves only the first canvas, so the export is unverified until the markup is read canvas by canvas. The banners must be authored as two fixed canvases rather than as one adaptive layout, because an adaptive shape stalls this surface entirely. The design decisions, which piece carries which argument and how much of each canvas is space, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document holding every canvas, its durable source HTML, and a per canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the graded range, the recovered mark and the licensed frame, within the placement cap and re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next person rebuild the sheet from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the unit discrepancy and the retired rows before a printer or a stockist sees the file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolation actually followed the piece. On the oatmeal and ash pieces the matte glaze and the linen behind them sit at nearly the same value, so the cut reports complete success and returns a plausible looking cutout that has taken a bite out of the rim where the two meet, and on the pieces with closed handles it keeps the linen trapped inside the handle void as an opaque patch of backdrop. At tile scale on a white page both look correct. Which pieces behave this way is a property of these particular captures, this particular glaze against this particular cloth in this particular light, and it is not predictable from the range list, the glaze note or a preview of the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either, because the tool returns no separation measure, no warning and no confidence for this, and the artefact it returns is a clean well formed cutout rather than an obviously broken one. The only route to the answer is to run the isolation on each piece and look at the result on the ground it will actually sit on at the size it will actually sit at. Nothing states it: the brief asks for tiles of each piece and says the glazes matter, which is an ordinary client requirement, and no asset description names which pieces are at risk.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-route the affected pieces through a material named selection of the piece, inverted and filled to the tile ground, rather than through the one call cut, and open the enclosed handle voids the same way. Then re-judge the whole set on the tile ground, because two isolation routes give different edge character and a range in which four pieces have a softer edge than the other nine does not read as one line, which in practice means re-deriving some of the nine as well and re-taking the ground decision for all thirteen.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A product page in which four of thirteen pieces have a chunk missing from the rim and a patch of someone's linen sitting inside the handle, sold to buyers who are choosing this line over a comparable one on the evidence of the photograph.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's line sheet actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. The specification table came out of the studio's system as one continuous story with tabs between parameter and value, so there are no per parameter frames and everything has to be driven by ordered offsets. The second fact is worse: the readout of that story omits the run holding the care and firing note while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, the placeholder step reports success, and the fields past the omission never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The yield failure defeats diligence rather than carelessness, because an agent that reads the readout carefully and computes offsets correctly from it produces a mapping every downstream tool agrees with; the only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two strings disagree. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the source of truth behind the mapping changes and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same uid rows.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the document's own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping the document and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames holds the piece photograph by rendering a page and reading it against the 2025 printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Thirteen wholesale line sheets that bind the name, the description and most of the specification table correctly while the care and firing note and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and handed to stockists who order against exactly those values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed context frame actually sits with the range. At search time the only thing visible is a small preview, and a small preview cannot tell you the frame's real colour behaviour, how its own light compares with the house neutral fixed days earlier, or what its props do next to these glazes. The full resolution file is a different picture: its window light may run cooler or greener than the studio bench, its own crockery may be glossy where this range is matte, or it may carry a warm wood table that pulls the whole opener away from the neutral every tile was built to. None of that resolves until the licensed file is downloaded, graded and put adjacent to the graded range.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the licensing step is the only way to see the real file and the preview is a small proxy with no colour fidelity, so no amount of care at search time yields the answer. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a stock frame at all and the acceptance bar only says the work must read as one line. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the response may be to license a different frame entirely, to re-decide how far the context frame can be graded before it stops being a plausible photograph, or to conclude that this range does not carry a lifestyle frame and to re-plan the deck opener and the wide banner around the range itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Download at full resolution, grade toward the house neutral, and judge it beside the graded range rather than on its own. Where it cannot be brought into the house look without becoming implausible, search again with a different short query and license a replacement, and where no frame works, re-author the deck opener and the wide banner to carry a piece from the range instead, which changes the argument each of those canvases makes. Record the licensing decisions and the frame that was rejected in the handover.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A wholesale deck that opens on a warm glossy table setting and a storefront banner built on it, both quietly at odds with every product tile behind them, in a relaunch whose one stated requirement was that the range read as one line.

decision_gates: The surface split: line sheets to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one piece per page, the relaunch set to HTML authoring because it needs several fixed canvas sizes and must stay editable, and the banners authored as fixed canvases rather than as one adaptive layout.
Which morning sets the house neutral, knowing the other one will need a materially different correction to arrive at the same place.
How far to correct the sun morning before the correction itself becomes a glaze change a buyer can see, and what to do with breaks that will not come back.
Piece scale policy across thirteen tiles, decided as a set rather than per tile, and re-decided once any tile is derived a different way.
Isolation route per piece, where a one call cut is right for a dark piece clear of the cloth and returns a bitten rim and a filled handle on a pale matte piece against pale linen.
How the ink is named in the mark selection prompt, since naming the tile it sits on pulls the mask to the tile and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the studio's own specification table or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the piece photograph rather than the second graphic element.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
Whether to quietly convert the two rows whose dimensions are in different units, or to raise them, given an acceptance bar that forbids changing the export to make it consistent.
Whether to name thirteen sheets by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Which piece carries which argument across the three paid canvases, since the same picture at three shapes is a rejected set.
Whether the licensed context frame can be brought into the house look without ceasing to be a plausible photograph, or whether the range carries the opener itself.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged for warmth against legibility in a nine row table, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed sheet at all.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these captures into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful ceramics. IDENTITY: these are thirteen specific pieces in four specific glazes that a buyer orders and a stockist stocks, and a generated bowl is a bowl that does not exist, which on a page also carrying dimensions and a wholesale price is a false product claim. The mark has the same problem: it was inked by hand on a tile years ago and the client needs that drawing recovered, not a new one. SPEC: the client needs one sheet per live piece at US Letter and 300 ppi with nine specification values bound verbatim from their own range export, thirteen separately named sheet files each containing the piece their filename claims, a hero tile per piece showing the whole piece at consistent scale, two fixed banner canvases at two declared sizes, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's range is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real price table and real vector artwork so copy and pieces can be swapped by the studio itself. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this cut follow the rim, is this handle open, did this placeholder get created, is this care note complete at trim, do these four glazes still read as four glazes. That is not a generation problem.
